blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Sapperton. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Sapperton, New Westminster: 33 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 2 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 6%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. By listings that is number 6 of 14 New Westminster communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the New Westminster total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Sapperton

Zoning correction — read first. 6680 (2001) districts are RT-2 through RT-2C plus RT-3/3A/3B ONLY — there are no RT-A/RT-B districts in New Westminster. Email check. The correct email is jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca.
The Columbia (Brewery District) — 258 Nelson's Court

By Wesgroup. A 26-storey tower with 242 homes per the developer-project report; MLS listing data for units in the building records Apartment/Condo sub-type and year built 2020, with access to the 10,000+ sq ft Club Central amenity space. One listing records pets "Cats OK." A published rental or age position: UNCONFIRMED. Note the project was announced under the address 285 Nelson's Court; the strata's operating address in listing data is 258 Nelson's Court.
The Sapperton (Sapperton at Brewery District) — 200 Nelson's Crescent

Strata plan EPS4191, managed by Assertive Northwest per the building's MLS data sheet, which records 114 total units in the development, freehold strata title, year built 2017, concrete high-rise construction, and pets allowed with restrictions. The project report describes it as a 14-storey tower of 114 condos.
The Keary — 230 Keary Street

By Wesgroup, the final ownership building in the Brewery District: a 30-storey mixed-use tower of 292 condominiums (studio to 3-bedroom) per the presale source. Status: current MLS listings at the address are assignment sales stating estimated completion in 2026–2027, while the presale source stated an expected completion of Spring 2025 — the completion date is UNCONFIRMED and the two sources conflict; treat purchases here as presale/assignment purchases under REDMA until the building's completion is confirmed. Published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Regal Manor — 316 Cedar Street

MLS listing data records the building name Regal Manor, Apartment/Condo sub-type, board sub-area Sapperton, year built 1976, and pets: No for the listed unit. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked. A published rental or age position: UNCONFIRMED.
Ashton Greene — 335 Cedar Street

MLS listing data records the building name Ashton Greene, Apartment/Condo sub-type, board sub-area Sapperton, year built 1982, an elevator building, and pets "Cats OK" for the listed unit. A published rental or age position: UNCONFIRMED.

items.t: Municipality and identity: Sapperton is the historic neighbourhood at the north-east end of the City of New Westminster, on the slope above the Fraser River between McBride Boulevard and the Coquitlam boundary at Brunette Creek, taking in Royal Columbian Hospital, Sapperton and Braid SkyTrain stations, Hume Park and the Brewery District. Exact board sub-area boundary roads are UNVERIFIED.
"Sapperton" is both the board (GVR) sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report and a City neighbourhood name (also written McBride-Sapperton).
New Westminster community level (medians published at community level only): condos & townhomes median $560,000, $587/sq ft, 95% sale-to-list, 27 days on market. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED.

Where the condo stock concentrates: two pockets — the Brewery District towers on Nelson's Court/Crescent and Keary Street across from Sapperton Station, and the older low-rise walk-ups on Cedar Street above East Columbia Street.

The hospital: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, is a Fraser Health regional referral hospital; its Jim Pattison Acute Care Tower (10 storeys, 388 beds) opened to patients on May 31, 2026.

Schools (SD40, address-based; locator run for 331 Richmond Street): Skwo:wech Elementary (K–5), École Glenbrook Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12). Skwo:wech Elementary at 331 Richmond Street opened June 6, 2022, replacing Richard McBride Elementary.

Transit and roads: Sapperton and Braid Expo Line stations; TransLink route 109 (New Westminster Station / Lougheed Station) runs East Columbia Street. Main roads: East Columbia Street, Brunette Avenue, McBride Boulevard and North Road, with Highway 1 access at the Brunette Interchange.
Nearby areas: Fraserview and Glenbrooke North west, The Heights (Victory Heights) north, Brunette below the hill, and Maillardville (Coquitlam) across Brunette Avenue.

items.t: The zoning error travels.

One master plan, four residential buildings, two tenures. The Brewery District's residential towers split evenly: The Columbia (242) and The Sapperton (114) are strata condos, The Nelson and The Westminster (187 homes) are rental — a buyer touring "the Brewery District" is looking at two different products on adjoining lots.

The Columbia has two addresses in the record. The project was announced at 285 Nelson's Court; listing data runs the strata at 258 Nelson's Court. Search both before concluding a unit's history is thin.

Cedar Manor's unit-count conflict dissolves in the City's own table. The 2009 Non-Market inventory's columns for 312 Hospital Street are 30 single + 20 disabled + 10 family = 60 total; later sources quoting "30" or "60" were reading different columns of the same row.
The newest elementary school is named for the river.

Sapperton Park predates the condos by a century. Sapperton Park at Columbia and Sherbrooke was built in 1907 and named for the Sappers; the neighbourhood name itself comes from the Royal Engineers' 1858 camp.

items.t: Sapperton is New Westminster's historic north-east neighbourhood, on the slope above the Fraser River between McBride Boulevard and the Coquitlam boundary at Brunette Creek, taking in Royal Columbian Hospital, Sapperton and Braid SkyTrain stations, Hume Park and the Brewery District on East Columbia Street. "Sapperton" is both the board (GVR) sub-area name and a City neighbourhood name (also McBride-Sapperton); the name comes from the Royal Engineers' 1858 camp — "Sappers' Town." Community figures (sub-area medians NOT published: UNVERIFIED): detached median $1,365,000, $504/sq ft, 94%, 35 days; attached median $560,000, $587/sq ft, 95%, 27 days.

Flood — a defining diligence item where met: the City floodplain study places the low Brunette River / Braid-side industrial land in Floodplain Zone 4, below the Flood Construction Level; the residential slope sits above it. Check the exact lot against City flood maps. Brunette is New Westminster ground (not a separate municipality).

Schools: SD40, address-based. Completed locator run documented in this area's own research (2026-10-21) for 331 Richmond Street returned Skwo:wech Elementary (K–5), École Glenbrook Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12). Skwo:wech Elementary (331 Richmond St, opened June 6, 2022) uses Ministry-listed naming as documented in the research. Other addresses: UNVERIFIED.

Transit/roads/health: Sapperton + Braid Expo Line stations; route 109 on East Columbia; East Columbia, Brunette Ave, McBride Blvd, North Road; Hwy 1 via Brunette Interchange. Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia St — regional referral hospital; its Jim Pattison Acute Care Tower (10 storeys, 388 beds) opened May 31, 2026.
Parks/library: Hume Park / Lower Hume Park, Brunette-Fraser Greenway, Sapperton Landing Park, Sapperton Park (1907); nearest library is the Main Branch, 716 6th Avenue, Uptown.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Sapperton

items.t: Form B diligence (the counted strata): SPA s.59 — fees, amounts owing, approved special levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement, most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page. Listing-level restriction lines are not bylaws — the Form B/registered bylaws govern, and at a 2025-built 9-lot complex the depreciation report cycle and CRF balance are still the documents to read.

Rental-restriction bylaws VOID: since Nov 24, 2022 — any directory "rentals not allowed" line for a Sapperton strata is VOID for long-term rentals, flagged in-entry wherever met (no counted complex here carries such a published line in the sources checked); short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw.

: Zoning Bylaw No. RS-1 (s.310): minimum site 557.40 m² / 6,000 sq ft, FSR 0.5, suites + laneway/carriage houses regulated in the same bylaw. OCP: "Our City 2041," Bylaw No. 7925, 2017 — Sapperton/Braid station areas are a Frequent Transit Development Area; 97 Braid St is designated Sapperton Green Transit-Oriented Mixed-Use Community, planned to connect to the City's Sapperton District Energy System (a future utility cost to ask about; connection for existing strata: UNCONFIRMED).

Taxes/rebates/financing: PTT 1% / 2% / 3% plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3M — any "Over $3M — 5%" line compresses 3% + 2%, flagged. Exemptions: first-time buyers full on first $500,000 at ≤$835,000, partial to $860,000; newly built full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000. Example (input: $560,000 community attached median, no exemption): $2,000 + $7,200 = $9,200. FTHB GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 — never March 12): 100% to $1M, phasing to $1.5M, max $50,000, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031; New Housing Rebate 36%, max $6,300, $350K–$450K phase-out; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. GST on new construction, not resales (Sapperton Living units are 2025-built — verify per-unit whether a sale is a developer sale or a resale, because that decides GST). Vancouver EHT does NOT apply.

items.t: One masterplan, two tenures. In the Brewery District, The Columbia (242) and The Sapperton (114) are strata condos while The Nelson and The Westminster (187) are rental — and the district's only counted townhouse complex, Sapperton Living (9 homes), sits on Keary Street between them.

The hospital tower is new this year. Royal Columbian's Jim Pattison Acute Care Tower opened May 31, 2026 (388 beds, new emergency/main entrance) — demand support near Sapperton Station, and a street-by-street parking/traffic check.
Sapperton Park predates the condos by a century — built 1907 and named for the Sappers; the neighbourhood name itself comes from the Royal Engineers' 1858 camp.

A 9-lot strata is over the depreciation threshold, barely. At 9 lots Sapperton Living must obtain 5-year depreciation reports (5+ lots since July 1, 2024) — a sub-5-lot complex would sit under it; lot count is therefore a diligence fact, not trivia.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Sapperton?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 33 condos and townhomes listed in Sapperton. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Sapperton a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Sapperton had a sales ratio of 6%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Sapperton from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 14 condos and townhomes sold in Sapperton over those 4 months, out of 261 in all of New Westminster.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Sapperton sell for?
faq.a: 42 condos sold in Sapperton between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $526,250.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Sapperton?
faq.a: The median was 37 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.3% of the last list price (12% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

Two pockets: the Brewery District across from Sapperton Station (The Columbia, 258 Nelson's Court, 2020, 242 homes; The Sapperton, 200 Nelson's Crescent, 2017, 114 units; The Keary, 230 Keary Street, completing — date UNCONFIRMED) and the older Cedar Street low-rises (Regal Manor, 316 Cedar Street, 1976; Ashton Greene, 335 Cedar Street, 1982).

faq.q: Is The Nelson or The Westminster a condo I can buy?
faq.a: No — both are Brewery District rental towers: Wesgroup states The Nelson is a rental building, and The Westminster was reported as 187 rental homes.

faq.q: Is Cedar Manor a 55+ condo building?
faq.a: Cedar Manor (312 Hospital Street) is in the City's Non-Market Housing inventory — it is not strata ownership at all, and the "60 vs 30" figures in circulation are the City table's total (60) versus its single-unit column (30). A market unit count is UNCONFIRMED and there is nothing to buy.

faq.q: What is happening at Braid Station?
faq.a: Sapperton Green: a 38.35-acre master-planned community proposed for 97 Braid Street — roughly 4,700 homes (including secured market rental and affordable housing), office, retail, a community centre and 7.9 acres of open space under an OCP designation and a Council-endorsed master plan concept. Construction timing is UNVERIFIED — do not pay today for unbuilt amenities.

faq.q: Did the hospital expansion change the area?
faq.a: The Jim Pattison Acute Care Tower at Royal Columbian Hospital opened May 31, 2026 — 388 beds, new emergency department and main entrance, expanded cardiac, surgical, maternity and newborn services. It supports demand near Sapperton Station and makes hospital-area parking and traffic a street-by-street check.

faq.q: Which townhouse complexes are verified in Sapperton?
faq.a: One counted: Sapperton Living, 339 Keary St — 9 strata townhomes, built 2025, Illuma / Sapperton Holdings Ltd, Freehold Strata on fresh listing title evidence. Fee-simple: none verified.
No — it is completed stock: built 2025 per listings and the directory, with completed units reselling on strata fees. A purchase runs on a Form B, not a disclosure statement.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Sapperton townhouse long-term?
faq.a: Yes — rental-restriction bylaws void since Nov 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw; read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.
